# InvalidOperandType

<Badge type="danger" text="error" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≥ 8.0" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Report an arithmetic or bitwise operation on an array or an object that the
code itself shows cannot take part in it. PHP throws a `TypeError`.

## Example

```php{4}
<?php
function bump(array $counts): int
{
    return $counts * 2;
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 4: Use a number here, not array.</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- An operand of `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`, `**`, `&`, `|`, `^`, `<<` or `>>`,
  or of the compound assignment of one of them.
- The type of the operand comes from native declarations only, and every
  member of it is an array, or every member of it is a class whose whole
  hierarchy is known.

## Exceptions (no report)

- `+` between arrays, which merges them: an array operand of `+` is
  reported only when the other operand is known and cannot be an array.
- An operand that may also be null, a scalar or an unresolved class.
- An object of a class that overloads operators: `GMP`, `BcMath\Number`,
  `FFI\CData` and their subclasses.
- A type that comes only from PHPDoc.

## Fix

None.

## PHP versions

Active from PHP 8.0, where these operations throw a `TypeError`.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "InvalidOperandType": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore InvalidOperandType
```
